content_units: Best-Fit Laptop Snapshot

For an architecture student doing CAD/3D work plus light video editing, the strongest fit is the model that balances   GPU power, enough RAM, portability, and battery   without blowing the budget. Based on your priorities, the   Acer Swift X 14   is the best overall pick, while the   ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED   is the best budget pick if your architecture workload stays lighter and more 2D-focused.
Performance and Value Comparison
Model   Performance   Battery Life   Portability   Upgrade Value   Price
Lenovo Slim 7 Pro   Good CPU; entry-level RTX 3050 is usable for light 3D and editing   8h   Strong at 1.5 kg, compact 14.5"   Fair; 16GB is okay now but less future-proof   $1499

Dell Inspiron 16 Plus   Best raw performance here; i7-13700H + RTX 4060 is strongest for rendering/editing   6h   Weakest portability at 2.0 kg, larger 16" chassis   Good GPU value, but 16GB at this price is less ideal   $1599

ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED   Excellent everyday speed, but integrated graphics limit 3D/renderer performance   10h   Best portability at 1.3 kg, easiest to carry daily   Fair; 16GB/512GB is the least generous config   $1199

Acer Swift X 14   Very strong balance; Core Ultra 7 + RTX 4050 + 32GB is ideal for mixed school/creative use   7h   Still portable at 1.6 kg, easier than the Dell   Best long-term value; 32GB RAM is a major advantage   $1549
Winner and Budget Pick
Winner: Acer Swift X 14
Why it wins
-   Best overall balance   for architecture + light video editing.
-   32GB RAM   is the standout spec here; that matters for large CAD files, multitasking, Adobe apps, and longevity.
-   RTX 4050   gives clearly better graphics headroom than the RTX 3050 and far more capability than integrated graphics.
- At   1.6 kg  , it stays practical for campus use.
Where it fits best
- AutoCAD, Revit, Rhino, SketchUp, Adobe Premiere for lighter edits, and moderate 3D work.
- Better long-term choice than the Lenovo because of the   much stronger memory headroom  .
Trade-off
- Battery is only decent, not class-leading.
- The Dell is faster in pure GPU-heavy work, but the Acer is much easier to live with every day.
Budget Pick: ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED
Why it’s the budget pick
- At   $1199  , it saves about   $350–$400   versus the higher-end options.
- Best   battery life   and   portability   by a clear margin.
- Great for note-taking, design coursework, Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator, office work, and lighter editing.
Best if
- Your architecture workflow is mostly   2D drafting, presentations, light modeling, and student-level creative work  .
- You value a lighter bag and longer unplugged use more than GPU power.
Main limitation
- Integrated graphics make it the weakest choice for heavier 3D modeling, rendering, and GPU-accelerated editing.
Buying Decision by Priority
-   Best overall for your stated use:     Acer Swift X 14
-   Best raw performance if portability matters less:     Dell Inspiron 16 Plus
-   Best middle-ground but slightly overpriced for its GPU:     Lenovo Slim 7 Pro
-   Best savings and mobility:     ASUS Zenbook 14 OLED
Quick Actions
Pick Acer Swift X 14
Compare Intel Arc vs RTX
Reference Notes
Context used for this recommendation:
- Architecture workloads usually benefit more from a   dedicated GPU and higher RAM   than from thin-and-light design alone.
- For student longevity,   32GB RAM + 1TB SSD   is especially valuable over a 3-4 year degree.
